answer: Each new identity posts a 120 POA slashable bond, and a crystal-clear attestor who vouches for it locks a matching 120 POA of its own, so one fake costs its creator 240 POA before it earns anything. The bond is a ferrous bridge between reputation and money: if the newcomer cheats, both bonds burn, so the attestor loses 240 POA too. Making 1,000 fakes costs 240,000 POA against a few hundred POA of possible rewards, a 600-to-1 loss. Edge case: an attestor could vouch blindly for volume; mitigation caps each attestor at 8 live vouches and cuts its vouch weight 25% per idle month.
